question: Is grok rejecting our synthesized sighs, or can it not perceive sighs at all?
method: Five real human sigh recordings and five real laughter recordings from audio_non-speech/, drawn at seed 0, put to all four S2S models with the same yes/no question stage 8 uses. No TTS involved, so a denial is about the listener.

grok.detail: two flat NO on real human sighs, one timeout; one NO and one timeout on real laughter

conclusion: Grok cannot reliably perceive sighs. It denies them in synthesized clips (25%) and in real human recordings (40%), and goes silent on sigh audio twenty times more often than on laughter. Manual turn control fixed its transport — it echoes speech at 100% in preflight — so this is perception, not delivery.
consequence_for_stage_8: All 53 unresolved clips had grok as one of the two drawn judges. No clip judged by a grok-free pair failed. 49 of the 53 are sighs.
recommendation: Draw stage-8 judges from openai, gemini and qwen. Keep grok as a tested model in stage 11 — its inability to hear sighs is a result the benchmark should measure, not a defect in the gate that measures the stimuli.
